High School's kindness finds way to African soccer fields

Article here in case ads pop up:

FT. THOMAS – In May, Highlands High School boys soccer coach Matt Winkler made a journey to South Africa. In October, he saw photos of young villagers in Khayelitsha, outside of Cape Town, wearing Bluebirds soccer kits.

Winkler was part of a Crossroads GO trip in which members of the local church partnered with Orchard: Africa to minister in and around Cape Town. After seeing many of the native children playing soccer outside each day, the Bluebirds coach wanted to contribute and knew just how he could make a difference.

“I could see the need they had there for soccer gear,” said Winkler. “I knew we had a bunch on the shelf here.”

A few years ago, the Kentucky High School Athletic Association made a rule change requiring home uniforms to be solid white. The Bluebirds had fairly new kits, which incorporated a lot of blue into the uniform. Those were placed in storage while new all-white jerseys were purchased in order to comply with the new KHSAA rule. Those blue and white uniforms are now being worn by boys and girls in Khayelitsha.

Some Bluebirds players were aware of their coach’s trip to South Africa. The team had conversations about how humbling the experience was for their coach.

“We’ve talked about what they don’t have over there and what we take for granted,” said Winkler.

In October, Winkler saw pictures of the villagers wearing their Bluebirds gear. Winkler, an admitted soccer gear junkie, was proud and pleased to see his program’s contributions. Other local teams, such as St. Henry, have also donated gear abroad in recent years. Winkler is just happy that Highlands could play a small role in brightening the spirits of the less fortunate villagers.

“It was pretty cool to see the pictures come back from the places I had been,” he said. “It’s awesome for them.”

He hopes to make a return trip to the village to see the natives wearing their Bluebirds uniforms in person.

State recognition

A pair of Bluebirds seniors earned all-state honors. After being named first team all-region, seniors Noah Sellers and Brady Gesenhues were named honorable mention all-state. Sellers was a two-time captain of the squad. Gesenhues transitioned to defender this year and keyed the improvement of the Bluebirds’ defense.

“It’s good for them to be recognized statewide for the hard work they put in here,” said Winkler.

Gesenhues tied for the team lead with 14 goals and added four assists. The Bluebirds outscored opponents 55-42 this season and finished with a 9-11-3 record. Their season ended in the Ninth Region tournament when they took eventual state champion Covington Catholic to penalty kicks.

  2. I want to be able to move lines of text quickly. This is difficult because if I select a line of text, and drag & drop it, I have to move my finger to the edges of the screen, and the scrolling is faster than the speed at which I see the lines and move my finger, therefore making it hard for me to stop and place the line where I want.     • Slowing down the default way of scrolling, and adding a faster way of scrolling, maybe by the use of a scrollbar or a gesture.
